b: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — For the last two years, a team of convention industry professionals, engineers, architects and financial and development consultants have evaluated the viability of building a major convention and events center at the Meadowlands Sports Complex. The proposed Meadowlands Convention Center would include 460,000 square feet of exhibition, meeting and ballroom space; a multipurpose venue capable of accommodating sporting and entertainment events; a 1,000-room headquarters hotel; and transportation, parking and infrastructure improvements.

The Scoping Assessment found that not only is the convention center viable, the $3.8 billion to $4.25 billion development will be a huge asset to the community in the form of 5,000 union construction jobs, more than 3,700 permanent jobs and a long-term business opportunity that is expected to bring in $30.4 billion.

“After two years of extensive research, independent analysis and consultation with some of the most respected professionals in the industry, the findings have been overwhelmingly positive,” Jim Kirkos, President and CEO of the Meadowlands Chamber and Meadowlands Live! Convention and Visitors Bureau, said. “What began as an ambitious vision has evolved into a thoroughly researched economic development opportunity that deserves serious consideration by the State of New Jersey.”
During the study, the Meadowlands Chamber and the Meadowlands 2040 Foundation commissioned research to find out how event organizers would respond to a new convention center in the region.

After surveying meeting and convention planners, researchers found that 90% of survey respondents were already familiar with the area — solidifying its reputation as a visitor destination. In addition, 80% of professionals would consider booking an event at the facility, and 45% indicated they were very likely to bring their events to the location.

“The most compelling finding of the entire Scoping Assessment came directly from the people who make the decisions about where conventions and meetings are held. When 80% of professional meeting planners surveyed tell you they would consider booking an event at the Meadowlands, that is an extraordinary validation of the market opportunity,” Kirkos explained. “These aren’t speculative opinions from project supporters. These are responses from the very professionals whose business will ultimately determine the success of this facility. The market is telling us there is an opportunity here, and we would be foolish not to listen.”
Now that the results of the assessment are in, the Meadowlands Convention Center project will move into the next step to get authorized for construction.

The Meadowlands Chamber is currently seeking assistance from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority and New Jersey Sports and Exposition Authority to plan the logistics of the project. During the next phase, issues related to construction budgeting and procurement; engineering and regulatory requirements; operational management and governance; public-private financing opportunities; and necessary state approvals will be addressed.

Also, the Meadowlands Chamber will host a series of briefings that will inform public officials, as well as business and labor leaders, on the findings of the Scoping Assessment and how the Meadowlands Convention Center will be brought to fruition, which Kirkos says will help secure the necessary buy-in to move forward.

“New Jersey has an opportunity to make a generational investment in its tourism and convention economy, but the next step must be guided by sound analysis and responsible decision-making. We have demonstrated the market opportunity, developed a comprehensive facility concept, evaluated critical infrastructure considerations and established a framework for moving forward,” Kirkos said. “What we are asking for now is not a commitment to build a multi-billion-dollar convention center. We are asking for the opportunity to complete the state-supervised work necessary to make an informed decision. Given the potential economic benefits, that is an investment in due diligence that New Jersey should be willing to make.”
